questions.question_english:
26. A traditional narrative art form from Telangana
involves painting stories from mythology on
long cloth scrolls using natural colors, presented
alongside oral storytelling by the Nakashi
community. What is this art form?
questions.explanation_english: Cheriyal Scroll Painting is a traditional art form from Telangana that involves the depiction of mythological stories on long scrolls. This art form is characterized by the use of natural colors and is often accompanied by oral storytelling, which is a significant cultural practice of the Nakashi community. The vibrant colors and intricate designs not only tell stories but also preserve the rich heritage of the region.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। चेरियाल स्क्रॉल पेंटिंग तेलंगाना की एक पारंपरिक कला रूप है, जो पौराणिक कथाओं की कहानियों को लंबे स्क्रॉल पर चित्रित करती है। यह कला प्राकृतिक रंगों का उपयोग करती है और इसे नकाशी समुदाय द्वारा मौखिक कहानी सुनाने के साथ प्रस्तुत किया जाता है। इसके जीवंत रंग और जटिल डिज़ाइन न केवल कहानियाँ सुनाते हैं, बल्कि क्षेत्र की समृद्ध विरासत को भी संरक्षित करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Cheriyal Scroll Painting
Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Cheriyal Scroll Painting is a traditional art form from Telangana that involves the depiction of mythological stories on long scrolls.

questions.question_english: 67. Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement regarding the Gig Economy in India?
options_english: Gig workers exclusively engage in short-term tasks or digital platform-mediated freelance jobs.
Gig work offers flexible working hours compared to structured traditional 9-to-5 employment models.
Gig workers automatically receive statutory provident fund contributions under current rules.
App-based food delivery executives and ride-hailing drivers represent primary platform gig workers.
questions.explanation_english: The statement that gig workers automatically receive statutory provident fund contributions under current rules is incorrect. Gig work typically involves flexible, short-term, or platform-based tasks performed by independent freelancers and app-based delivery partners. Unlike traditional formal sector employees, gig workers in India are classified as independent contractors and do not automatically receive statutory provident fund contributions from platform employers. Therefore, the claim that gig workers automatically receive statutory provident funds is false.
